[Triton] Fix E8M0 scale decoding (#11624)

Fix by @Maratyszcza

E8M0 byte `0` represents `2^-127`, and byte `255` represents NaN.
Several software decoders treated these as zero or infinity. Correct
both encodings across compiler lowering, the interpreter, standalone
upcasts, packed Hopper FP4 layouts, and scaled reductions. For example,
a 128-term dot product of BF16 `2^112` and FP8 `256` with scale byte `0`
must return `1`; the old decoder returns `0`.

The fix covers integer E8M0 scales with FP4 E2M1 and FP8 E4M3/E5M2
values. Scaled reductions also cover BF16 and FP32 inputs. BF16 and FP32
decoding preserve the minimum value; FP16 still rounds it to zero. H100
software decomposition is affected, including two-scaled FP8 matmuls.
Native NVIDIA block-scaled MMA keeps its existing path, and a zero
floating-point scale remains zero.

Numeric software decoders zero-extend and shift the scale byte, preserve
the BF16/FP32 minimum with an integer maximum, and use `fma(scale, +0,
scale)` to turn the infinity encoding into NaN. The generic FP16 path
omits the minimum correction because that value rounds to zero. The FMA
precedes FP16 narrowing; generic dot decomposition also decodes before
scale broadcasting. Packed Hopper decoding applies the same operations
to two BF16 lanes per instruction. The interpreter and AMD software
upcasts also normalize NaN scales. Signed-byte storage is reinterpreted
as unsigned before widening: byte `0x80` encodes `+2`, not `-2`.

The remaining exceptions preserve their existing contracts:

- Software `dot_scaled` omits explicit scale-NaN handling under
`fast_math=True`; Triton-to-Gluon's existing decomposition supports only
this mode.
- Native AMD conversion instructions consume encoded scales;
`dot_scaled` keeps its existing NaN mask after conversion. Direct
hardware upcasts retain the hardware decoding path, with added NaN-scale
regression tests.
- Saturating library upcasts restore scale NaNs after clamping, which
would otherwise erase them. An earlier FMA would be redundant.
- FPSan uses integer payload arithmetic, including the native UE8M0
conversion. Torch references retain an independent bit-mask decoder.

### Native Blackwell scale decoding

The shared `upcast_ue8m0_scale` helper uses
[`cvt.rn.bf16x2.ue8m0x2`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/#data-movement-and-conversion-instructions-cvt)
for BF16 on Blackwell. It decodes two scale bytes per instruction,
preserving both the minimum value and NaN. Scalar scales, FP16/FP32
outputs, and earlier GPUs use the portable decoder. FPSan preserves the
same integer payloads for both implementations.

Compared with the correct software decoder in [Merge main and resolve
MXFP test
imports](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/commit/3bfb37d69a8264a854582ddd583b4aeaebf0d8cb),
[[NVIDIA] Use native UE8M0 decoding in kernel
helpers](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/commit/ab6ac038ade3d0fb93693d7d7615673d940005d3)
lowers large FP4 → BF16 upcast latency by **3.7%** on GB300. Large E5M2
→ BF16 is **1.1% slower**; standalone scale decoding is unchanged.
Compiler `dot_scaled` decomposition keeps the max/FMA decoder: inserting
this packed inline assembly there caused extra layout and multiplication
work.

stages, and FP32 accumulation/output. `fast_math=False` unless labeled.
The two-scaled FP8 case uses software decomposition on H100 and native

Timings use 32 launches per CUDA graph, 200 ms warmup, and 12
alternating AB/BA pairs with approximately 50 ms per arm, followed by a
fresh-process repeat. Times are medians; changes are medians of paired
ratios. No clock locking or cache flushing. Allocation, compilation,
module loading, and graph creation are excluded. Binaries at the linked
revisions were checked against the measured kernels; changed `fast_math`

usage; timing differences in these controls do not establish a speedup.

Affected GB300 mixed-input cases with a scaled left operand and
`fast_math=False` save 28–31 KiB of shared memory per block. H100 shared

BF16 × FP4 case adds eight local bytes per thread, and some cases add
registers. Local storage is allocated capacity, not measured spill
traffic; the tables show these changes explicitly.

### Packed Hopper FP4 layouts

The packed Hopper decoder applies the minimum clamp and NaN-restoring
FMA to both BF16 lanes, preserving its four-scale packing. A 128-term
BF16 `2^118` × FP4 `4` matmul with scale byte `0` returns `1`. Scale
byte `255` produces NaN for nonzero FP4 inputs, where the old helper
produced infinity.

Compare the minimum-only decoder in [[KERNELS] Preserve minimum E8M0
scales in Hopper
layouts](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/commit/0a1a9a317f5ea90a6b3fa9a3b2794aecd1ea637c)
with [[Triton] Complete E8M0 scale
decoding](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/commit/2f3e1c6a2927cf5687f5872361d65f8cbcb5f943).
These measurements isolate the additional NaN handling with the same
native compiler. **At most 1.08% additional latency across two runs;
register, local/shared-memory, scratch, and warmed Torch memory usage
are unchanged.** A fresh build of the merged branch, with only the
decoder changes reverted for the baseline, reproduces the machine code
and resource counts of all 16 measured kernels.

Inputs are BF16 × FP4 with group-32 E8M0 scales `124`–`129` and FP32
output. Tiles are `128×(32·warps)×128`. Regular kernels use one pipeline
stage; persistent kernels use three stages with four warps and two with
eight warps. A separate three-stage regular configuration produces
incorrect results in both versions and on unmodified upstream code
predating this PR; it is excluded from these timings. All timed outputs
match an independent Torch reference exactly. Timing uses 32 launches
per CUDA graph and 12 alternating AB/BA pairs, approximately 50 ms per
arm, repeated in a fresh process.

### Validation

- A fresh build of the current head passes 145 library tests, 16
original minimum/zero-scale compiler regressions, 4,134 adversarial
matrix cases, and three FPSan tests on GB300. Coverage includes every
UE8M0 byte, signed-byte storage, both operand orders, FP16 boundaries,
and NaN-times-zero. NaN scales are excluded under `fast_math`. Native
and portable FPSan decoding agree for all 256 bytes.
- All 26 final GPU-code comparisons match: 16 `dot_scaled` kernels and
two FP32 reductions retain the software baseline's machine code and
resources; eight standalone upcast/decoder kernels reproduce the native
measurements above. Separate offline H100 checks retain identical
machine code and resources for 22 matmul/upcast kernels. The current
library matmul callers use the tile upcast helper only before Blackwell,
so they do not select its new native path.
- Hopper coverage includes every FP4 value with every scale byte, both
axes, four/eight warps, signed zero, and subnormals. Public
regular/persistent matmuls return NaN for scale `255`; the previous
helper returned infinity. The unchanged interpreter and Triton-to-Gluon
paths previously passed all 15 interpreter tests and 12 boundary cases.
Reduction tests check forward results and gradients.
- Rebuilt native code passes seven focused compiler files: three AMD
lowering files, generic max/FMA decoding, and common/AMD/NVIDIA FPSan.
Added runtime tests cover NaN scales with zero/nonzero FP4/E4M3/E5M2
inputs on CDNA3 and CDNA4. AMD runtime correctness has not been tested
locally on this revision; AMD performance was not measured.

Below CUDA capability 8.9, tests skip unsupported E4M3 conversion. E5M2
still checks NaN forward decoding and finite gradients; its NaN-gradient
case excludes the existing legacy FP8 downcast limitation.

The separate [[KERNELS] Reduce FP4/FP8 upcast
overhead](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/11644) remains
stacked on this correctness fix.

### Reviewer's guide

- `include/triton/Dialect/TritonGPU`, `lib/Dialect/TritonGPU`: decode
minimum and NaN scales before broadcasting; declare the Math dialect
dependency.
- `lib/Dialect/TritonInstrument`, `third_party/amd`: matching FPSan

in AMD software upcasts; preserve native AMD exponent carriers and their
final NaN mask.
- `python/triton/runtime`, `python/triton/tools`,
`python/triton_kernels`: NaN-preserving interpreter decoding, unsigned
scale extension in Gluon, a shared Torch reference decoder, and
consistent decoding in upcasts, packed Hopper FP4 layouts, and
reductions. The shared helper explicitly names UE8M0 and uses native
BF16 conversion on Blackwell.
- `python/test`, `python/tutorials`, `third_party/amd/python/test`,
`test`: reference reuse and boundary coverage across scale formats,
operand orders, and native AMD controls.

[KERNELS] Support unscaled FP8 E4M3 matmul with FP16/BF16 (#11652)

Unscaled E4M3FN paired with FP16/BF16 currently fails
`triton_kernels.matmul` dtype or Hopper weight-layout checks. Both
kernels now widen only the FP8 tile to its partner's dtype before
`tl.dot`, preserving input storage and FP16 precision. The multiply uses
16-bit tensor cores.

Persistent kernels prefer FP8 on the MMA's lhs and use smaller K tiles
on Hopper. Account for staged inputs, widened RHS tiles and epilogue
scratch separately, leave Blackwell TMEM headroom, and select a fitting
epilogue before clamping stages. Keep gathered-input offsets separate
from the aligned base pointer when flattening persistent loops. AMD
sizes unscaled K tiles using the wider operand, so mixed FP8/16-bit
tiles fit gfx942 shared memory.

With the [unchanged upstream
compiler](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/commit/2074a1b8a5cd283ce584f8ebca825c4f0b215fc1),
**520 mixed-dtype cases pass on H100 and 264 on GB300; all fail against
the base library**. The existing `test_op` grid now covers all four
mixed dtype pairs, both weight layouts, regular/persistent kernels,
bias, scaling and gather/scatter. Eight focused cases retain
memory-limit, default-planner and exact FP16 precision coverage. The 256
H100 / 128 GB300 skips are unchanged inapplicable inner-expert
combinations. Two existing FP16 gather/split-K and ragged-K cases also
pass on both libraries and GPUs.

AMD runtime CI passes all 132 newly enabled mixed cases on
[gfx942](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/actions/runs/34404235031/job/102643281846),
[gfx950](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/actions/runs/34404235031/job/102643281882),
and [gfx950 with ROCm
10.1](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/actions/runs/34404235031/job/102643281817),
including the 32 gfx942 cases that exceeded shared memory before the
tile-size fix. HIP retains its unsupported persistent/TMA exclusion.

### BF16

**Relative speed: BF16 × BF16 = 1.00×. Higher is faster.** Speed is
baseline latency divided by measured latency.

| GPU | M × N × K | FP8 × BF16 | BF16 × FP8 | FP8 × FP8 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| H100 | 16 × 4096 × 4096 | 0.95× | 0.73× | 1.19× |
| H100 | 128 × 4096 × 4096 | 0.86× | 1.06× | 1.21× |
| H100 | 2048 × 4096 × 4096 | 0.85× | 0.85× | 1.90× |

operand](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/commit/a00f0cc854c41c23d895f2aedb7d14dc15849dbf).
